line: Thirtieth of December, couch and a quilt
Swiping back through the year I built
Blurry sunsets, a lopsided cake
The first long run I swore I'd never make
A screenshot of a "yes" I almost didn't send
A photo of me laughing with a brand new friend
Twelve months fit inside my hand
More than I remember, more than I planned
It wasn't a big year, but it was mine
Small brave things, one at a time
No trophy, no spotlight, no big parade
Just a hundred little days I made
You don't need a big year
To have a good one, it's true
Look how much light you caught
In this camera roll, in you
There's a gap in March, not a photo at all
Heavy weeks I barely recall
Then April's back with a crooked selfie
Coffee with Mom, a walk, a bakery
I kept the hard parts out of frame
But they're part of the year all the same
Swipe to the end, the screen goes bright
It's snowing now, and I'm alright
It wasn't a big year, but it was mine
Small brave things, one at a time
No trophy, no spotlight, no big parade
Just a hundred little days I made
You don't need a big year

In this camera roll, in you
